_readme: Frame and install copy for the Frame Types screen. Edit name, desc (one sentence), bestFor (bullets), and sees (what the homeowner sees). installType must be an id in data/install.json. Choosing a frame on an estimate line sets that install type and its per-window labor price: zbar retrofit / Z-bar uses standard (Jump Frame, $360), block uses block ($380), nailfin uses stucco-fin (Nail Fin RnR Stucco, $400). diagram is the picture key: zbar, block, or nailfin. The pictures are original SVGs in js/pages/frame-types.js. The license note at the top of that file lists the guides that were reviewed and not copied.

types.name: Retrofit / Z-bar
types.desc: The new window sets into the old frame, and the stucco stays.
bestFor: A sound stucco wall where the old frame is solid and close to square
A replacement that should be done without cutting the stucco
sees: Glass that is a little smaller, because the old frame stays
The new frame sitting inside the old one
A Z-bar on the outside, covering the joint at the stucco
Sealant where the Z-bar meets the stucco

types.name: Block frame
types.desc: A plain box screws into the opening. Nothing sticks out past the wall.
bestFor: An opening that is already clear, with the old frame gone
A pocket built for a box frame, when the trim is finished on its own
sees: No fin on the outside of the wall
The new frame set flush in the opening
Screws through the frame into the studs
Sealant in the joint around the frame
Interior trim, plus a separate piece of exterior trim

types.name: Nail fin
types.desc: The fin nails to the sheathing, then stucco or siding covers it.
bestFor: New construction, before the stucco or siding goes on
A full tear-out when the old frame is rotted, rusted, or out of square
sees: The old frame gone, so the glass size is kept
A nailing fin fastened to the sheathing
New stucco or siding covering that fin
